title: Decentralize commit path and introduce lightweight KV-cache compaction
creator: Priya Menon
description: Context: Our continuous-batching commit path currently funnels most requests through a single global coordinator that holds a coarse lock while performing KV cache lookups and commit handoffs. This has created a contention hotspot during high concurrency workloads and complicates dependency upgrades (notably grpc and the async runtime). Goal: Reduce contention and make the commit handoff path resilient to partial KV cache compaction runs. Deliverables: (1) a decentralized commit handoff that routes commits to per-shard workers, (2) a lightweight background compaction pass for the KV cache that opportunistically removes stale slot entries and coalesces nearby ranges, and (3) compatibility shims so we can upgrade grpc/async runtime incrementally without broad rollout risk.
technical_notes: Design summary: - Introduce per-shard commit queues keyed by KV shard id to avoid a global commit lock. Each queue has a small bounded worker pool. - Replace long synchronous compaction pauses with an incremental compactor running at low priority and limited wall-time per tick. - Expose a compact_hint API from the cache read path to let the commit worker signal hot ranges that should be fast-checked before write-through. - Add feature-flagged compatibility shim for grpc channel draining to allow mixed-version nodes during the dependency upgrade window. Trade-offs: increases code complexity in the shard-routing layer but reduces tail latency and makes stepwise rollouts safe. Implementation constraints: keep public runtime API stable; avoid changing RPC shape in canary release. Benchmarks: target >=20% throughput improvement under 95th percentile concurrency workloads and 10-25% reduction in p95 token latency for 8k-seq customers.

review_feedback: PM review (Leah Ortiz): prefer conservative defaults for compactor to avoid surprises for customers — agreed to expose config toggles
Security review (note): compactor touches cache metadata only, no user data purging — security OK but requested audit logs for compaction errors
Perf review (Marcus Li): suggested adding a metric for 'compactable_bytes' to drive automatic tuning — added to monitoring TODO
Design review (Alyssa Chen): recommended explicit backpressure signals from commit workers to upstream batcher when shard queues saturate
notes: Rollout plan: feature flagged at runtime; canary on 3 dedicated nodes for 48h -> 25% cluster rollout -> full cluster if stable
Rollback plan: flip feature flag, drain per-shard workers gracefully by completing inflight commits; use cached snapshots if needed
Follow-ups: consider migrating compactor metrics into Optimize to drive automatic compaction thresholds based on workload patterns
